fields.expected: I'm an undergraduate at Johns Hopkins studying Applied Mathematics & Statistics and Economics, and most of my work has been building machine learning and full-stack systems for real users. Right now I work on the machine learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system at Summer Atlantic Capital / SAC Nexus, where I own the event-ingestion pipeline, a versioned FastAPI detection service, temporal sequence modeling over event streams, and a learning-to-rank layer for prioritizing alerts. The part I care about most there is operational usefulness: an anomaly system that fires too often just creates a second problem, so prioritization and explanation quality matter as much as model performance. Before that I worked with Intelehealth on AI and data systems for rural telemedicine, including a resource-availability scoring pipeline across 32 villages and an evaluation framework comparing LLM-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard. I also co-founded Open Health Intelligence and built ClarityAtlas, an iOS health app in Swift and SwiftUI with a passive sleep-estimation system, shipped into a live Hopkins pilot with 30+ users.
